   and no division by the skein variable is used.

Let
$$S=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1}))$$
be the Dubrovnik coefficient ring, and let
$$T=S[q^{\pm1}]/(q-q^{-1}-z).$$
In $T$ put $\rho=a$, $\delta=d$, and $z_B=q-q^{-1}$. Then the natural
map $S\to T$ is injective and $T$ is a free $S$-module with basis $1,q$.
Moreover, the BMW coefficient relation
$$z_B(\delta-1)=\rho-\rho^{-1}$$
holds, and the substitution $a=\rho$, $z_D=z_B$, $d=\delta$ converts
the BMW skein, curl, adjacent untwisting, and loop coefficients to the
Dubrovnik relations in the specified chart: $D_+-D_-=z_D(D_0-D_\infty)$,
the curl factors are $a,a^{-1}$, and a disjoint trivial circle contributes
$d$. Here $D_0$ is through and $D_\infty$ is cup-cap. No skein parameter is
divided out.

Let
$$R_D=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1})),$$
where $z$ is not inverted. A nonempty unoriented regular link diagram is a
finite generic planar projection of one or more circles with only transverse
double crossings and an over/under marking at each crossing. Use the crossing
chart in which the over-strand runs southwest to northeast. Its $D_0$
smoothing joins the left endpoints and the right endpoints (the through
pairing), and its $D_\infty$ smoothing joins the two top endpoints and the two
bottom endpoints (the cup-cap pairing). Thus $D_0$ is the orientation-preserving
smoothing when both crossing strands point downward and the displayed crossing
has positive determinant sign. These are respectively the $A$- and
$B$-smoothings in the stated bracket chart. A positive
curl is a type-I kink whose oriented crossing has determinant sign $+1$; a
negative curl has determinant sign $-1$. The sign is unchanged if the
orientation of the whole component is reversed.

The Dubrovnik regular-isotopy evaluation $P$ is normalized by
$P(\varnothing)=1$, $P(K\sqcup\bigcirc)=dP(K)$, positive and negative curl
factors $a$ and $a^{-1}$, and
$$P(D_+)-P(D_-)=z\bigl(P(D_0)-P(D_\infty)\bigr).$$
Here $D_+$ and $D_-$ differ only by switching the displayed crossing. For a
nonempty oriented link diagram $K$, let $c(K)$ be its number of components and
let $w(K)$ be the sum of the determinant crossing signs. Define
$$D_K(a,z)=d^{-1}P(K),$$
$$L_K(A,Z)=-i^{w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}D_K(-iA,iZ),\qquad i^2=-1,$$
and
$$F_K(A,Z)=A^{-w(K)}L_K(A,Z).$$
Thus $D$ has unknot value $1$, and the universal relation defining $R_D$ is
retained even when $z$ is not invertible. These are conventions and
normalizations; ambient-isotopy invariance of $F$ is a separate theorem.

Let $n\ge0$ and let $\beta=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$ be a geometric braid with
the fixed real basepoints $q_j=((2j-n-1)/(4(n+1)),0)$ and endpoint
permutation $\pi$, as in [[def-geometric-braid-with-setwise-endpoints]].
Identify the disk with $\{x\in\mathbb C:|x|<1\}$ and put
$$V=(D^\circ\times[0,1])/((x,1)\sim(x,0)).$$
The quotient and its topology use [[def-product-topology]] and the circle
$\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ of [[def-circle-as-real-line-mod-integers]].
The interval images
$$s_j=\{[(z_j(t),t)]:0\le t\le1\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}(\beta)=\bigcup_{j=1}^n s_j$$
are the **closure in the open solid torus**. In general an individual
$s_j$ is an interval image, not a closed circle: its last point is the
first point of $s_{\pi(j)}$.

**Components and orientation.** For a cycle
$(j,\pi(j),\ldots,\pi^{k-1}(j))$ concatenate these $k$ strand maps in
that order, with parameter in $[0,k]$. Their endpoints agree in $V$,
so the concatenation factors through $\mathbb R/k\mathbb Z$.
It is injective on this circle: points at distinct nonintegral heights
can agree only when their parameters have the same fractional part,
and the distinct strands at that height have distinct disk coordinates;
at integral heights only the specified adjacent endpoints agree.
Thus each cycle gives an embedded circle. Different cycles give
disjoint circles, and every strand belongs to exactly one cycle.
These circles are precisely the connected components of the closure.
The orientation is increasing concatenation parameter. In particular
the number of components equals the number of cycles of $\pi$.

**The standard axis and fixed framing.** In
$S^3=\{(z,w)\in\mathbb C^2:|z|^2+|w|^2=1\}$, as in
[[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]], set
$$A=\{(0,w):|w|=1\},\qquad P_\theta=\{(z,w)\in S^3:z\ne0,\ \arg z=\theta\}.$$
Fix the following particular diffeomorphism, including its disk framing:
$$\varphi([(x,t)])=  \bigl(\sqrt{1-|x|^2}\,e^{2\pi it},x\bigr):  V\longrightarrow S^3\setminus A.$$
Its inverse has disk coordinate $x=w$ and circle coordinate
$[t]=[\arg z/(2\pi)]$. Every $P_\theta$ is consequently an open disk.
The **raw topological oriented closure** is
$$\widehat\beta_{\mathrm{top}}=\varphi(\operatorname{cl}(\beta)).$$
This explicit $\varphi$ is part of the construction; the definition
does not allow an arbitrary page-preserving change of framing.

**Page intersections and smooth representatives.** The whole closure
meets every page in exactly $n$ points. A component belonging to a
$\pi$-cycle of length $k$ meets each page in exactly $k$ points:
at any fractional height it uses exactly those $k$ distinct strands.
The page coordinate of its concatenation is $[t]$, for
$t\in\mathbb R/k\mathbb Z$, so its oriented degree is $+k$.
If all disk-coordinate strand maps are smooth and have all positive-order derivatives
zero at their endpoints, their cycle concatenations have matching jets
at every seam. The page coordinate has nonzero derivative, so the
result is a smooth embedding of disjoint oriented circles, in the
sense of [[def-smooth-embedding]]. For an endpoint-flat smooth braid, its literal $\varphi$-image is therefore a smooth oriented link and is denoted $\widehat\beta$.

**Closure in the smooth oriented-link category.** The raw image need not be smooth, even if individual strands are smooth but their endpoint jets fail to match at the cycle seams. For an arbitrary continuous braid, assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and choose a smooth representative $\beta_s$ by [[lem-every-geometric-braid-is-braid-isotopic-to-a-smooth-braid]]. Make it endpoint-flat by composing all disk-coordinate strands with a fixed smooth nondecreasing $\psi:I\to I$, equal to $0$ near $0$ and $1$ near $1$. Interpolation of height maps $(1-u)t+u\psi(t)$ is an endpoint-fixed braid isotopy, because every strand is evaluated at the same height. The smooth-category closure of $\beta$ is the oriented-link isotopy class of this chosen model's literal $\varphi$-image; when a subset is needed, use that chosen closed-braid representative. Independence of the representative is proved by [[lem-closure-depends-only-on-the-braid-isotopy-class]]. Page and cycle properties refer to the chosen constructed closed braid, with the same number of strands and endpoint permutation as $\beta$.

If $\beta$ already has smooth strands with matching cycle-seam jets, in particular if it is endpoint-flat, its literal raw image is a smooth link and is retained as $\widehat\beta$. The raw quotient, fixed $\varphi$, finite cycles, page counts and trivial closures remain choice-free. Finite elementary words have explicit smooth endpoint-flat models, so forming their literal closures also requires no choice assumption; $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used for the general continuous-representative convention and its independence theorem.

**The trivial closure.** For the constant braid its circles are
$\{(\sqrt{1-q_j^2}e^{2\pi it},q_j):[t]\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\}$.
They are latitudes of the sphere
$S=\{(z,w)\in S^3:\operatorname{Im}w=0\}$, with
$\operatorname{Re}w=q_j$. Each northern cap
$C_j=\{p\in S:\operatorname{Re}w(p)\ge q_j\}$ is a smooth disk:
stereographic coordinates on $S$ give radius
$\sqrt{(1-q_j)/(1+q_j)}$ for this cap. To make their spanning disks
disjoint, let $e$ be the unit vector in the $\operatorname{Im}w$
direction, set $\varepsilon=\pi/16$ and
$f_j(p)=\varepsilon(\operatorname{Re}w(p)-q_j)$ on $C_j$, and use
$$F_j(p)=\cos(f_j(p))p+\sin(f_j(p))e.$$
The boundary is fixed. The tubular parametrization
$(p,s)\mapsto\cos(s)p+\sin(s)e$ is injective for $|s|<\pi/2$,
and $0\le f_j<\pi/8$. On overlapping caps, if $q_i<q_j$ then
$f_i-f_j=\varepsilon(q_j-q_i)>0$, so their graphs are disjoint.
Thus these are pairwise disjoint smooth spanning disks. The trivial
$n$-braid closes to the oriented $n$-component unlink; for $n=1$
this is the unknot.

At $n=0$ all strand and cycle unions are empty, every page has zero intersections,
and the closure is the empty link. The basepoint list and disk constructions
above then have no entries.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $B_n=\langle\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}\mid\text{Artin
relators}\rangle$ be the braid group of the Artin presentation
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]); recall that $B_0$ and $B_1$
are trivial. The **exponent sum** is the unique homomorphism

$$e_n:B_n\longrightarrow\mathbb Z,\qquad e_n(\sigma_i)=1\quad(1\le i\le n-1),$$

where $\mathbb Z$ is the additive group of integers. It is well defined because
every defining relator of the Artin presentation has exponent sum $0$: the
braid relator $\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}$
has both sides of exponent sum $3$, and each far-commutation relator has both
sides of exponent sum $2$, so the assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto1$ kills all
relators, and [[thm-von-dyck]] applies. It is surjective for $n\ge2$ and it is
the trivial map on the trivial group $B_1$. For every Artin word
$\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_k}^{\varepsilon_k}$ one has
$e_n(\beta)=\sum_{r=1}^k\varepsilon_r$ independently of the word, and
$e_n(\beta^{-1})=-e_n(\beta)$. **Caveat:** $e_n$ is the composite of the
abelianisation $B_n\to B_n^{\mathrm{ab}}$ with a surjection onto the free cyclic
group $\mathbb Z$ (for $n\ge2$): since the target is abelian, every commutator is sent to $0$, so $e_n$ factors through $B_n/[B_n,B_n]$ ([[def-abelianisation-of-a-group]]). No normal form, Garside structure or
faithfulness statement is used anywhere.

Substitution in [F3] gives $-(-1)^1=1$. By [F6], $L_{\bigcirc}(A,Z)=-i^0(-1)^1D_{\bigcirc}(-iA,iZ)=1$, so $F_{\bigcirc}(ia,-iz)=1$, agreeing with the algorithm output.

A positive curl multiplies $D$ by $a$ and raises $w$ by one, so the product $a^{-w}D$ is unchanged; a negative curl multiplies $D$ by $a^{-1}$ and lowers $w$ by one, with the same cancellation. To obtain the corresponding Kauffman factors directly from [F6], substitute $a_D=-iA$ and $z_D=iZ$ in $D$. A positive curl preserves $c$, raises $w$ by one, and multiplies $D$ by $a_D$, so it multiplies $L$ by $i a_D=A$. A negative curl lowers $w$ by one and multiplies $D$ by $a_D^{-1}$, so it multiplies $L$ by $i^{-1}a_D^{-1}=A^{-1}$. Thus $A^{-(w+1)}A L=A^{-w}L$ and $A^{-(w-1)}A^{-1}L=A^{-w}L$. These are algebraic calculations for the fixed diagram and its two curls, using only [F1] and the definitions. Thus both local curl cases preserve the normalized value.

The identity $2$-braid closes to the two-component unlink, so [F1] gives $P=d^2$ and $D=P/d=d$. Hence [F2] gives $\tau_2(1)=d^{-2}d^2=1$. By [F7], its writhe is $0$ and $c=2$, so [F3] returns $-d$. The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal A$ be a compact smooth
planar annulus and set
$X=\operatorname{int}(\mathcal A)\times(-1,1)
=\operatorname{int}(\mathcal A\times[-1,1])$, the interior of a solid torus.
A regular annular diagram is a finite immersed union of circles in
$\operatorname{int}(\mathcal A)$ with only finitely many transverse double
points, no triple points, and over/under data from the interval coordinate.
The **blackboard framing** is the normal strip lying in the annulus. A specified
framing differs from it on each component by an integer full-twist correction,
measured by the winding number of its normal direction relative to the
blackboard normal. Count the correction positively for an A-type full twist,
whose local curl has A-smoothing equal to the straight strip with one
contractible circle; count the opposite B-type twist negatively. Every framed
link in $X$ admits a regular annular diagram. The correction may be recorded
as signed full-twist marks on diagram arcs; its total is additive when arcs
are concatenated.

If two framed links in $X$ are ambient isotopic through links in $X$, their
regular annular diagrams are related by finitely many annular planar isotopies
and local oriented Reidemeister I, II, and III moves in disks contained in
$\operatorname{int}(\mathcal A)$. Reidemeister II and III and planar isotopy
preserve the blackboard framing; an A-type or B-type Reidemeister I move
changes it by one corresponding full twist, so the correction integer changes
by the opposite twist. For framed links in $S^3$, every link also admits a
regular planar diagram, and any two diagrams of ambient-isotopic framed links
are related by a finite planar-isotopy/Reidemeister sequence with the same
framing-correction rule.

Let $M$ be a smooth oriented $3$-manifold and let $L$ be a framed unoriented
link in its interior with a specified component. A positive full framing twist is the local blackboard
curl whose $A$-smoothing is the straight strip with one additional
zero-framed trivial circle; a negative full framing twist is the curl whose
$B$-smoothing is the straight strip with one additional zero-framed trivial
circle. Write $L^+$ and $L^-$ for the links obtained by inserting these twists
on one component. With $R=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$ and
$\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$, the module classes satisfy
$$
[L^+]=-A^3[L],\qquad [L^-]=-A^{-3}[L].
$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and let $R=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$ and
$\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. For a nonempty framed unoriented link $L$ in $S^3$,
choose a regular planar diagram $D$ of its core. Let $m_j\in\mathbb Z$ be
the full-twist correction on the $j$th component from the blackboard framing
of $D$ to the specified framing of $L$, counting an A-type twist positively
and its inverse negatively as in the framed diagram calculus, and put
$m=\sum_jm_j$. For a state
$S$ of $D$, let $a(S)$ and $b(S)$ be its numbers of A- and B-smoothings and
$|S|$ its number of resulting circles. The assignment
$$
E(\varnothing)=1,\qquad
E(L)=\delta(-A^3)^m\sum_{S}A^{a(S)-b(S)}\delta^{|S|-1}
$$
is independent of the diagram and twist corrections and extends
$R$-linearly to a map $E:\mathcal K_A(S^3)\to R$ satisfying
$E([\varnothing])=1$.

derivations.claim: We prove by induction on the number of crossings of a regular diagram for a blackboard-framed link that its class is a scalar multiple of $[\varnothing]$. If the diagram has a crossing, the crossing relation in [F1] expresses its class as the sum of the two smoothing classes with coefficients $A$ and $A^{-1}$. The skein convention gives each smoothing its blackboard framing, and each has one fewer crossing, so the induction applies. A crossingless diagram is a finite disjoint union of planar circles. Choose an innermost circle; its planar disk has no other component in its interior and is disjoint from the remaining link. Its blackboard framing is the zero framing, so [F1] removes it with factor $\delta$. Remove this component and repeat; the crossingless link reduces to a scalar multiple of the empty link. For a general framed link, [F2] supplies a diagram and [F3], applied finitely many times to its framing-correction integer, reduces its class to a scalar multiple of the corresponding blackboard-framed diagram. Hence every class lies in $R[\varnothing]$.

Define $\phi:R\to\mathcal K_A(S^3)$ by $\phi(r)=r[\varnothing]$. Step 1.1 makes $\phi$ surjective. If $\phi(r)=0$, $R$-linearity and $E([\varnothing])=1$ give $r=E(\phi(r))=E(0)=0$. Thus $\phi$ is injective as well as surjective, so the empty class is a free $R$-module generator.
The trivial-circle relation in [F1], with $L=\varnothing$, gives $[O]=\delta[\varnothing]$, as claimed.

citations.quote:
Fix an even integer $p\ge4$ and a primitive $2p$-th root of unity $A\in\mathbb C$. Put

$$
\zeta=A^2,\qquad q=-\zeta,\qquad r=p/2,\qquad
\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}=q+q^{-1}.
$$

The coefficient field after specialization is $\mathbb C$, and the Kauffman bracket loop coefficient is $\delta$ in the framed-link relation $[L\sqcup O]=\delta[L]$. Define the quantum integers by $[0]=0$, $[1]=1$, and $[j+1]=\delta[j]-[j-1]$ for $j\ge1$. Since $q^2=A^4$ has order $r\ge2$, these quantum integers also satisfy

$$
[j]=\frac{q^j-q^{-j}}{q-q^{-1}}=(-1)^{j-1}\frac{A^{2j}-A^{-2j}}{A^2-A^{-2}}.
$$

The BHMV simple-label convention is the finite set

$$
\mathcal J_p=\{0,1,\ldots,r-2\}.
$$

The pivotal loop and coefficient conventions throughout this page are the displayed $\delta$ and $\mathbb C$; no zero quantum integer is inverted.

Let $R$ be a nonzero commutative ring with unit, $\delta\in R$, and suppose $[2],\ldots,[n]$ are units. The projector $p_n$ of [[def-temperley-lieb-jones-wenzl-recursion-over-unit-denominators]] has coefficient $1$ on the identity diagram, is nonzero and idempotent, and is annihilated on both sides by each $U_i$ for $1\le i<n$. Its corner is $p_n\mathrm{TL}_n p_n=R p_n$, so it is the unique idempotent with identity coefficient $1$ and those two-sided annihilation conditions. For $n\ge1$,

$$\operatorname{ptr}_n(p_n)=\frac{[n+1]}{[n]}p_{n-1},\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_n(p_n)=[n+1].$$

Only the displayed denominator units are assumed; $\delta$ need not be a unit.

For any commutative ring $R$, loop value $\delta\in R$, and $n\ge0$, the unnormalized trace of [[def-temperley-lieb-closure-trace-and-partial-trace]] satisfies

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n(xy)=\operatorname{Tr}_n(yx),\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}(x\otimes1)=\delta\operatorname{Tr}_n(x)$$

for $x,y\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$. For $n\ge1$ and $x\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$, it also satisfies

$$\operatorname{Tr}_{n+1}((x\otimes1)U_n)=\operatorname{Tr}_n(x),$$

where $U_n$ is the cup-cap generator on the last two strands of $\mathrm{TL}_{n+1}$. For $n\ge1$, $x\in\mathrm{TL}_{n-1}$ and $h\in\mathrm{TL}_n$,

$$\operatorname{Tr}_n\bigl(h(x\otimes1)\bigr)=\operatorname{Tr}_{n-1}\bigl(\operatorname{ptr}_n(h)x\bigr).$$

No division by $\delta$ occurs.

Work over $\mathbb C$ with a fixed loop parameter $\delta$. Let $\mathcal T_\delta$ be the strict Temperley–Lieb diagram category of [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]]: its objects are $n\in\mathbb N$, and its morphism space $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_\delta}(m,n)$ is the complex span of the noncrossing matching diagrams with $m$ bottom and $n$ top boundary points, composed by stacking and loop removal.

For a basis endomorphism $D:n\to n$, let $c(D)$ be the number of components after joining each top point to the corresponding bottom point outside the rectangle. Define the unnormalized closure trace by
$$\operatorname{Tr}_n(D)=\delta^{c(D)},$$
and extend linearly. This definition is valid for every $\delta\in\mathbb C$, including $\delta=0$.

For $m,n\in\mathbb N$, the subspace of **negligible morphisms** is
$$\mathcal N_\delta(m,n)= \{f\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_\delta}(m,n): \operatorname{Tr}_m(g\circ f)=0\text{ for every }g\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_\delta}(n,m)\}.$$
This definition specifies subspaces only. Their closure under composition and tensor product, and hence the quotient category, are supplied separately.

derivations.claim: For $p\ge6$, one has $r\ge3$, so every denominator $[2],\ldots,[r-1]$ is nonzero and therefore invertible in $\mathbb C$. By [F2] and [F3], the recursion defines nonzero idempotents through $p_{r-1}$ and gives $\operatorname{Tr}_{r-1}(p_{r-1})=[r]=0$. For $p=4$, $r=2$ and $p_{r-1}=p_1=1_1$ is the initial projector; its closure is $\delta=[2]=0$, so the same conclusion holds without using a rank-two denominator.

For any $g\in\mathrm{TL}_{r-1}$, [F3] gives $p_{r-1}gp_{r-1}=\lambda p_{r-1}$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb C$. Cyclicity [F4] gives $\operatorname{Tr}(gp_{r-1})=\operatorname{Tr}(p_{r-1}gp_{r-1})=\lambda\operatorname{Tr}(p_{r-1})=0$. Thus $p_{r-1}$ is negligible by [F5].

The recursive formula for $p_r$ requires the inverse of $[r]$, which does not exist because $[r]=0$. Therefore that formula has no value at this step; in particular, assigning a value by cancelling a zero denominator is not part of the recursion. This leaves open the separate existence question for normalized idempotents constructed by other methods.

r=3: [2]=−1 is invertible, p2 exists, Tr(p2)=[3]=0, and the next recursion uses [3]=0.

$$

$$

$$
\mathcal J_p=\{0,1,\ldots,r-2\}.
$$

The pivotal loop and coefficient conventions throughout this page are the displayed $\delta$ and $\mathbb C$; no zero quantum integer is inverted.

Fix even $p\ge4$, a primitive $2p$-th root $A$, and $r=p/2$. In the Temperley–Lieb diagram category over $\mathbb C$ with loop value $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$, call $f:m\to n$ negligible when $\operatorname{Tr}_m(g\circ f)=0$ for every reverse morphism $g:n\to m$, where $\operatorname{Tr}$ is the unnormalized diagram-closure trace. A tensor ideal is a family of linear subspaces of the morphism spaces closed under composition on either side and tensor product on either side by arbitrary morphisms. The negligible morphisms form a tensor ideal. This ideal is generated, as a tensor ideal, by the Jones–Wenzl projector $p_{r-1}$, defined by the standard recursion through its first zero quantum integer; in particular the quotient has precisely the surviving projector labels $0,\ldots,r-2$.

Use all $\ell\ge3$, $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, $s=e^{\pi i/(2\ell)}$, $\delta=q+q^{-1}$ and the full tilting category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]]. Put $V=\Delta(1)$ and let $P_0$ be its trivial-channel projector in $V\otimes V=\Delta(2)\oplus\Delta(0)$. The maps

$$\rho_n:\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal T_\ell}(V^{\otimes n}),\qquad U_i\longmapsto\delta P_{0,i,i+1}$$

are well defined. Their composite with the negligible quotient has kernel exactly the embedded boundary ideal $I_n=(p_{\ell-1})$ and induces

$$\mathrm{TL}_n(\mathbb C,\delta)/I_n\ \cong\ \operatorname{End}_{\mathcal T_\ell/\mathcal N_\ell}(V^{\otimes n}).$$

Equivalently the target is the full centralizer on a chosen sum of the retained tilting summands. The unreduced map does **not** kill $p_{\ell-1}$: its image is the nonzero simple $\Delta(\ell-1)$.

The precise categorical comparison is with the additive Karoubi negligible quotient of $\mathrm{TL}(-\delta)$, equipped with its ordinary diagram braiding $c=s1+s^{-1}e$ and with planar pivotal structure multiplied by tensor parity $(-1)^n$. This is ribbon-equivalent to $\mathcal T_\ell/\mathcal N_\ell$. Its endomorphism algebras are identified with positive-loop TL algebras by $U_i=-e_i$. Its pivotal dimensions are $[a+1]_q$, and its twists on retained labels are $s^{a(a+2)}$. The quantum self-duality cup/cap have loop $-\delta$ and Frobenius–Schur sign $-1$, whereas the parity-corrected pivotal closure has value $+\delta$ on $V$. Thus no equivalence of the unmodified positive-loop unoriented **pivotal** TL category is asserted.

On the highest-weight-$2$ and trivial prequotient channels, the quantum crossing eigenvalues are $s,-s^{-3}$; the Hecke element $T_i=qU_i-1=-s c_i^{-1}$ has eigenvalues $-1,q^2$. The highest-weight-$2$ channel is retained only when $\ell\ge4$. Pivotal traces, twists and all framed ribbon closures agree under the stated corrected comparison. Assume countable choice only when invoking the cited free framed-tangle evaluation theorem; the local matrix and path arguments use no choice axiom.

For every $\ell\ge3$, let $\mathcal T_\ell$ be the full finite-dimensional integrable type-1 tilting category of [[def-temperley-lieb-rank-one-lusztig-tilting-category]], and $\mathcal N_\ell$ its negligible ideal. The quotient with the same objects and morphism spaces $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_\ell}(X,Y)/\mathcal N_\ell(X,Y)$ is a finite semisimple ribbon category. Its simple objects are exactly $T(0),\ldots,T(\ell-2)$, of pivotal dimensions $[a+1]_q$, and

$$[T(a)][T(b)]=\sum_{\substack{|a-b|\le c\le\min(a+b,2\ell-4-a-b)\\c\equiv a+b\ (2)}}[T(c)]\qquad(0\le a,b\le\ell-2).$$

Here a fusion category means a $\mathbb C$-linear rigid semisimple monoidal category with simple unit and finitely many simple isomorphism classes. The quotient is spherical with the specified positive pivotal dimensions and inherits the full ribbon structure, including even $\ell$.

Let $\ell\ge3$, $q=e^{\pi i/\ell}$, and let $\mathcal C_\ell$ be the standard ribbon semisimplification of finite-dimensional integrable type-1 tilting modules for Lusztig's divided-power $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, using the positive-trace quantum ribbon convention. Then $\mathcal C_\ell$ is modular, with simples $a=0,\ldots,\ell-2$, dimensions $d_a=\sin((a+1)\pi/\ell)/\sin(\pi/\ell)$, twists $\theta_a=q^{a(a+2)/2}$, and

$$s_{ab}=\frac{\sin((a+1)(b+1)\pi/\ell)}{\sin(\pi/\ell)},\qquad S_{ab}=\sqrt{\frac2\ell}\sin\frac{(a+1)(b+1)\pi}{\ell}.$$

Let $\mathcal C$ be a complex finite semisimple rigid tensor category with simple unit $\mathbf 1$ and a finite set $I$ of isomorphism classes of simple objects. Fix a braiding $c$ and a ribbon twist $\theta$. The induced pivotal map is $j_X=u_X\theta_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$, where $u$ is the Drinfeld morphism of [[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Throughout this pair we use the associated spherical pivotal structure: $j$ is part of the data, and sphericality means $\dim_j(X)=\dim_j(X^\vee)$ for every object, as in [[def-spherical-structure]]. Its trace is $\operatorname{tr}_j(f)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_Xf)$ for $f\in\operatorname{End}(X)$.

Write $0$ for the unit label and $i^*$ for the dual of $i$. Put $N_{ij}^k=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}(k,i\otimes j)$, $d_i=\operatorname{tr}_j(1_i)$, and $s_{ij}=\operatorname{tr}_j(c_{j,i}c_{i,j})$. Define $D^2=\sum_{i\in I}d_i^2$. The unnormalized Hopf-link matrix is $s=(s_{ij})$. The ribbon fusion category is **modular** when $s$ is invertible. When $D^2\ne0$, either square root $D$ defines the normalized matrix $S=s/D$; for a modular category, [[lem-modular-hopf-matrix-squared]] proves this nonvanishing. No positivity of the general $d_i$ or of $D$ is assumed.

Fix an even integer $p\ge4$, a primitive $2p$-th root $A\in\mathbb C$, $r=p/2$, and loop value $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$. Let $\mathcal T_\delta$ be the complex Temperley–Lieb diagram category with objects the nonnegative integers and morphisms finite linear combinations of perfect matchings of bottom and top boundary points with no intersecting arcs. Compose by stacking and remove each closed component with factor $\delta$. Define $\mathcal N_\delta(m,n)$ to be the subspace of morphisms $f:m\to n$ such that $\operatorname{Tr}_m(g\circ f)=0$ for every reverse morphism $g:n\to m$, where $\operatorname{Tr}$ is the unnormalized diagram-closure trace. Form the quotient category with the same objects and morphism spaces $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_\delta}(m,n)/\mathcal N_\delta(m,n)$. Its additive envelope adjoins finite formal direct sums, with matrix morphisms and matrix composition. Its idempotent completion adjoins objects $(X,e)$ for idempotents $e\in\operatorname{End}(X)$ with $e^2=e$, and morphisms $(X,e)\to(Y,f)$ are morphisms $a:X\to Y$ satisfying $a=fae$. Juxtaposition, planar cup-cap duality, and the induced trace descend to this completed quotient. This definition makes no assertion that it is semisimple, that its simple objects have a specified label set, or that any braid, twist, or modularity identities hold.

derivations.claim: If $r=2$, then $p=4$, $\delta=0$, and the sole proposed retained label is $0$. The boundary projector is $p_1=1_1$ and has zero trace. The tensor ideal it generates contains $1_n=1_1\otimes1_{n-1}$ for every $n\ge1$. Therefore every morphism with a positive source or target is zero in the quotient, because it factors through the corresponding identity. The endomorphism space of object $0$ is $\mathbb C$, and its trace is the identity, so it is non-negligible. The quotient's additive idempotent completion is thus finite-dimensional vector spaces with one self-dual simple $0$. Its fusion is $0\otimes0=0$, its unit twist is $1$, and its Hopf-link matrix is the $1\times1$ matrix $(1)$, which is invertible.

Suppose $r\ge3$ and first take the canonical root $A_0=e^{\pi i/(2r)}$, so $q_0=A_0^2=e^{\pi i/r}$ and the BHMV loop is $-(q_0+q_0^{-1})$. By [F3], the diagram quotient with its parity-corrected pivotal structure is ribbon-equivalent to the positive-pivotal quotient of [F4]–[F5]. Thus the quotient has exactly the labels $0,\ldots,r-2$, the displayed truncated fusion multiplicities, self-dual simples, and a nondegenerate Hopf-link matrix for that corrected pivotal structure.

On the semisimple quotient define $\varepsilon_{p_a}=(-1)^a\,1_{p_a}$. This is a monoidal natural automorphism: each retained summand $p_c$ of $p_a\otimes p_b$ has $c\equiv a+b\pmod2$ by [F4], so $\varepsilon_{p_c}=\varepsilon_{p_a}\varepsilon_{p_b}$; it is dual-compatible because every $p_a$ is self-dual. The planar pivotal structure is $\varepsilon$ times the parity-corrected one of [F3]. Multiplying a pivotal structure $j$ by a dual-compatible monoidal automorphism $\varepsilon$ changes the twist $u^{-1}j$ to $\varepsilon\theta$, preserves balancing by monoidality, and preserves dual compatibility; hence the planar convention is also ribbon. Its dimensions are $d_a=(-1)^a d_a^+$, which equal the BHMV recurrence value $[a+1]$: the sequence $v_j=(-1)^{j-1}[j]_{q_0}$ has $v_0=0$, $v_1=1$ and satisfies $v_{j+1}=-(q_0+q_0^{-1})v_j-v_{j-1}$, so uniqueness of the recurrence gives $v_j=[j]$ for the BHMV loop. Its simple twists are $\theta_a=(-1)^a\theta_a^+=(-1)^aA_0^{a(a+2)}$. Its unnormalized Hopf-link entries are $s_{ab}=\varepsilon_a\varepsilon_b s_{ab}^+$, since the pivotal trace on $p_a\otimes p_b$ is multiplied by $\varepsilon_a\varepsilon_b$. Therefore its Hopf-link matrix is obtained from the invertible matrix in [F5] by multiplying row $a$ and column $b$ by $(-1)^a$ and $(-1)^b$, so it remains invertible. The criterion in [F6] proves modularity.

For any primitive $A$, write $A=A_0^k$ with $\gcd(k,4r)=1$. The automorphism of the cyclotomic field $\mathbb Q(A_0)$ sending $A_0$ to $A$ transports the finite diagram coefficients, the recursively defined projectors, the braiding and twist matrices, and the Hopf-link matrix. By [F7], every fixed Hom space is finite-dimensional, so this transport preserves all ranks and nonzero determinants. The fusion multiplicities are dimensions of these finite Hom spaces and so are unchanged under the field automorphism and extension to $\mathbb C$. Thus the canonical-root result applies to every primitive $2p$-th root with the exact stated BHMV convention; in particular $\theta_a=(-1)^aA^{a(a+2)}$.

derivations.claim: If $r=2$, then $p=4$, $\delta=0$, and the sole proposed retained label is $0$. The boundary projector is $p_1=1_1$ and has zero trace. Therefore every morphism with a positive source or target is zero in the quotient, because it factors through the corresponding identity. The endomorphism space of object $0$ is $\mathbb C$, and its trace is the identity, so it is non-negligible. The quotient's additive idempotent completion is thus finite-dimensional vector spaces with one self-dual simple $0$. Specialize the framed-link Kauffman bracket skein module of $H$ to the coefficient field and root fixed above. For $x\in\mathcal K_A(H)$ and $y\in\mathcal K_A(H')$, define the handlebody pairing $B_\Sigma(x,y)$ by gluing the two framed skeins and evaluating the resulting closed marked three-manifold with the normalized root surgery invariant. Define

$$
\operatorname{Rad}(B_\Sigma)=\{x\in\mathcal K_A(H):B_\Sigma(x,y)=0\text{ for every }y\in\mathcal K_A(H')\},
\qquad

Let $H$ be a handlebody with a fixed finite trivalent spine $G$, and let every edge carry one of the labels $0,\ldots,r-2$. Call a labeling admissible when the three labels at each trivalent vertex satisfy the root fusion rule. In the radical-quotient state space of $H$, the states represented by admissible labeled spines span, and the set of such labelings is finite. K_0=\lambda_1,\qquad

This finite linear-algebra identity is exactly the sewing contraction in the imported gluing theorem and is independent of the chosen dual bases.

citations.quote:
Fix an even integer $p\ge4$ and a primitive $2p$-th root of unity $A\in\mathbb C$. Put

$$
\zeta=A^2,\qquad q=-\zeta,\qquad r=p/2,\qquad
\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}=q+q^{-1}.
$$

The coefficient field after specialization is $\mathbb C$, and the Kauffman bracket loop coefficient is $\delta$ in the framed-link relation $[L\sqcup O]=\delta[L]$. Define the quantum integers by $[0]=0$, $[1]=1$, and $[j+1]=\delta[j]-[j-1]$ for $j\ge1$. Since $q^2=A^4$ has order $r\ge2$, these quantum integers also satisfy

$$
[j]=\frac{q^j-q^{-j}}{q-q^{-1}}=(-1)^{j-1}\frac{A^{2j}-A^{-2j}}{A^2-A^{-2}}.
$$

The BHMV simple-label convention is the finite set

$$
\mathcal J_p=\{0,1,\ldots,r-2\}.
$$

The pivotal loop and coefficient conventions throughout this page are the displayed $\delta$ and $\mathbb C$; no zero quantum integer is inverted.

derivations.claim: Here $r=3$, $q=-A^2$ has $q^2$ of order three, and $q+q^{-1}=-1$. Thus $\delta=-1$, $[2]=\delta=-1$, and $[3]=\delta[2]-[1]=(-1)(-1)-1=0$.

The recursion for $p_3$ requires division by $[3]$. Since $[3]=0$ in $\mathbb C$, no multiplicative inverse exists, so this recursive expression is undefined. In particular, cancellation cannot assign it a value. The calculation refutes the asserted universal continuation; it makes no claim that a projector at rank three cannot be constructed by a different method.

$$

The pivotal loop and coefficient conventions throughout this page are the displayed $\delta$ and $\mathbb C$; no zero quantum integer is inverted.

Let $p\ge4$ be even, let $A$ be a primitive $2p$-th root of unity, and use the quantum integers and Temperley–Lieb loop value $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ specified above. Write $r=p/2$. The standard Jones–Wenzl recursion defines nonzero idempotents $p_n$ for $0\le n\le r-1$; their unnormalized closure traces are $[n+1]$. In particular, $p_{r-1}$ has trace zero and is negligible, while the next standard recursive formula for $p_r$ is undefined because its denominator is $[r]=0$. This statement concerns that recursion and does not assert that no differently constructed normalized idempotent can exist at rank $r$.

Let $p\ge4$ be even, $A\in\mathbb C$ a primitive $2p$-th root, and $r=p/2$. In the BHMV Temperley–Lieb quotient with loop value $\delta=-A^2-A^{-2}$ and planar pivotal trace, the complete simple-label set is $\{0,1,\ldots,r-2\}$, represented by the surviving Jones–Wenzl projectors $p_a$ obtained from the standard recursion using unit denominators $[2],\ldots,[a]$. Every simple is self-dual. Its fusion multiplicities are

$$
N_{ab}^{c}=1
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
|a-b|\le c\le\min(a+b,\,2r-4-a-b)
\ \text{and }a+b+c\text{ is even},
$$

and are zero otherwise. With the BHMV overcrossing map $c_i=A1_i+A^{-1}U_i$, where $U_i$ is the cup-cap generator, the full-framing ribbon structure has planar quantum dimensions $d_a=[a+1]$ and simple-object twists $\theta_a=(-1)^aA^{a(a+2)}$. Here the quantum integers use the fixed BHMV recurrence. The unnormalized Hopf-link matrix, whose $(a,b)$ entry is the pivotal trace of the double braiding on $p_a\otimes p_b$, is nondegenerate. Here modular means that this finite semisimple ribbon category has an invertible unnormalized Hopf-link matrix.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and let $R=\mathbb Z[A^{\pm1}]$. Identify
the solid torus with $\mathcal A\times[-1,1]$, where $\mathcal A$ is a planar
annulus. A simple closed curve is called essential if it does not bound a disk
in $\mathcal A$. Every framed link in this product admits a regular annular
diagram and an integer framing correction from its blackboard framing. Let
$z$ be one blackboard-framed annular core curve, and for $n\geq1$ let $z^n$
denote $n$ parallel copies of that curve, with $z^0$ the empty link. In the polynomial
ring $R[z]$, $z$ is also the formal variable sent to the core class $[z]$.
Then the classes $[z^n]$, $n\geq0$, form an $R$-basis of
$\mathcal K_A(\mathcal A\times[-1,1])$. Equivalently, the map
$J:R[z]\to\mathcal K_A(\mathcal A\times[-1,1])$ sending $z^n$ to $[z^n]$ is
an $R$-module isomorphism.

For the fixed root parameter, the normalized double-handlebody pairing on the admissible spine states of a marked handlebody is nondegenerate after quotienting by its radical. The inverse pairing defines the sewing map for gluing along a closed marked surface, and these maps satisfy the stated weighted Lagrangian anomaly correction.

derivations.claim: At $p=4$, $r=2$ and $r-2=0$, so the displayed label set is exactly $\{0\}$. At $p=6$, $r=3$ and $r-2=1$, so it is exactly $\{0,1\}$.

At $p=6$, $\delta=-1$, $p_2=1_2+U_1$, and $e_0=-U_1$ is an idempotent isomorphic to the tensor unit. Since $p_2$ is negligible by [F2], the decomposition $1_2=p_2+e_0$ gives $1\otimes1\cong0$ in the quotient. This verifies the stated fusion calculation.

By [F6] the torus dimension is the number of these basis labels, namely $r-1$. Step1.1 gives one label for $p=4$ and two labels for $p=6$, so the dimensions are $1$ and $2$. Together with the retained local fusion calculation in step2.1 this proves every Example clause. No polynomial skein basis before radical quotient is confused with the finite TQFT basis.

citations.quote:
Use coordinates $(z,t)\in\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ on oriented $\mathbb R^3$, with $t$ increasing upward. A knot is a smooth embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ with the orientation of $S^1$. A strict Morse presentation is one for which $t|_K$ has nondegenerate critical points, meaning its second derivative in a local coordinate is nonzero there, and pairwise distinct critical values. Write $t_{\min}:=\min_{x\in K}t(x)$, $t_{\max}:=\max_{x\in K}t(x)$, and $r(K)$ for the number of local maxima. A parenthesized $q$-braid is a smooth braid with $q$ strands, each strictly increasing in $t$, together with an ordered binary parenthesization of its lower endpoints and an ordered binary parenthesization of its upper endpoints.

For $n\ge0$, a degree-$n$ chord diagram is an oriented circle with $n$ disjoint unordered pairs of distinct points, called chords. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr}}$ be the rational vector space on these diagrams modulo 4T, and let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}}$ be its quotient by 1T as well. A 4T relation fixes one chord $pq$ and another chord endpoint $r$, moves the other endpoint of the second chord to just before or after $p$ and just before or after $q$, and takes the alternating sum of those four diagrams. A chord is isolated when it intersects no other chord, where intersection means that chord endpoints alternate around the circle; 1T sets every such diagram to zero. Put $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{fr/un}}_{\mathbb C}:=\prod_{n\ge0}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr/un}}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C)$, with multiplication induced by connected sum of diagrams and unit the empty diagram. For $q$ ordered upward strands, let $\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q)$ be the completion of the associative algebra generated by $t_{ij}=t_{ji}$ for $1\le i<j\le q$, with relations $[t_{ij},t_{kl}]=0$ when $i,j,k,l$ are distinct and $[t_{ij},t_{ik}+t_{jk}]=0$ when $i,j,k$ are distinct. The generator $t_{ij}$ is a horizontal chord joining strands $i$ and $j$; multiplication stacks diagrams from bottom to top.

More generally, a compact strict Morse tangle $T$ is a compact oriented smooth one-dimensional submanifold of $\mathbb C\times[a,b]$, with distinct boundary points on the planes $t=a$ and $t=b$, transverse to those planes, and with nondegenerate interior critical points of height having distinct critical values. A tangle chord diagram is a finite set of unordered pairs of distinct interior points on the oriented tangle skeleton. Its 4T relation is the same local alternating relation as above on the skeleton. The unframed tangle quotient also sets to zero any chord whose endpoints are consecutive in the order along the same skeleton component; for a circle the order is cyclic and for an arc it is linear. The completed degreewise tangle diagram space is denoted $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}(T)$.

The unframed configuration series of a strict Morse presentation $K$ is the formal degreewise series
$$
Z(K):=\sum_{m\ge0}\frac1{(2\pi i)^m}\int_{t_{\min}<t_m<\cdots<t_1<t_{\max}}\ \sum_{P}(-1)^{\downarrow(P)}[D_P]_{\mathrm{un}}\bigwedge_{j=1}^m\frac{dz_j-dz'_j}{z_j-z'_j}\ \in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}.
$$
The ordered simplex is divided into chambers by the critical values of $t|_K$. In each chamber, $P$ ranges over choices, at each level $t_j$, of an unordered pair of distinct points $(z_j,t_j),(z'_j,t_j)$ of $K$. The diagram $D_P$ joins the corresponding preimages on the oriented parameter circle. The integer $\downarrow(P)$ counts endpoints at which $t$ decreases along the orientation of $K$. The differential form is pulled back to the chamber by the selected local branches. The degree-zero term is the empty diagram with coefficient $1$; the displayed integrals are interpreted as improper integrals on each chamber.

For a compact strict Morse tangle $T$, $Z(T)$ is given by the same formula with $T$ in place of $K$, the interval $(a,b)$ in place of $(t_{\min},t_{\max})$, the chord diagrams on the tangle skeleton in place of circle diagrams, and the corresponding unframed tangle quotient in place of $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}$. A parenthesized braid is a special case with no interior critical points.

For a parenthesized braid path $\gamma$ in the configuration space of $q$ distinct complex points, define its Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov (KZ) series by the degreewise iterated-integral holonomy of
$$\Omega_q=\frac1{2\pi i}\sum_{1\le i<j\le q}t_{ij}\,d\log(z_i-z_j).$$
Explicitly, if $\gamma:[0,1]\to\operatorname{Conf}_q(\mathbb C)$ is an ordinary path with noncolliding endpoints, its holonomy is
$$1+\sum_{m\ge1}\int_{0<t_m<\cdots<t_1<1}\gamma^*\Omega_q(t_1)\cdots\gamma^*\Omega_q(t_m).$$
A tangential endpoint is a limiting collision configuration together with a specified nonzero first-order direction of approach for each colliding cluster. When endpoints have such clusters prescribed by the parenthesizations, the holonomy is the constant term after removing the local logarithmic factors $\exp(t_{ij}\log\varepsilon/(2\pi i))$ at each tangential endpoint. A change between the two parenthesizations of three consecutive strands is encoded by the regularized transport $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}$.

For parenthesized braids the KZ holonomy takes values in the framed strand algebra, where only tangled 4T is imposed; passing from a closed framed strand diagram to an unframed knot applies the quotient by isolated-chord 1T. Fix a standard hump $H$ by starting with the two-critical-point unknot and inserting one local birth of a maximum-minimum pair; thus $H$ has two local maxima. The normalized unframed Kontsevich series of $K$ is
$$
I(K):=Z(K)\,Z(H)^{-r(K)}\in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C},
$$
The normalization uses one copy of $Z(H)$ for each local maximum; its degree-zero term is $1$, so its inverse is interpreted in the product completion. This definition makes no assertion that the unnormalized KZ coefficients are rational or that equal Kontsevich series separate knot types.

The following figure illustrates the positive Artin generator $\sigma_1$ and parenthesization conventions. Height increases upward, the right-bottom strand is the overstrand under the determinant crossing convention, and the labels at the ends record the ordered parenthesizations; no proof below relies on the drawing.

derivations.claim: For a three-strand configuration, translation and positive scaling put the three points at $0,z,1$. The $t_{13}$ term of $\Omega_3$ is constant in these coordinates, while $d\log(z_1-z_2)=d\log z$ and $d\log(z_2-z_3)=d\log(z-1)$. Thus the reduced equation is exactly the displayed equation with residues $a$ at $0$ and $b$ at $1$.

Near $z=0$, substitute $G_0(z)=f(z)z^a$ with $f(z)=1+\sum_{n\ge1}f_nz^n$. Comparing coefficients in the differential equation gives $(n-\operatorname{ad}_a)f_n=-b\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}f_j$, where $\operatorname{ad}_a(x)=[a,x]$. On the degree-$N$ quotient, $\operatorname{ad}_a$ raises degree and is nilpotent, so $(n-\operatorname{ad}_a)^{-1}=\sum_{s=0}^{N}(\operatorname{ad}_a)^s/n^{s+1}$ is defined. This determines every $f_n$ uniquely. If $S_n=\sum_{j=0}^n\|f_j\|$ in any norm on the finite-dimensional quotient, the recurrence gives $S_n\le(1+C_N/n)S_{n-1}$ for a constant $C_N$; hence $S_n$ grows at most polynomially, and $f$ converges for $|z|<1$. It solves the equation by termwise differentiation.

Replacing $z$ by $1-z$ and interchanging $a,b$ gives the same recurrence at $z=1$ and uniquely constructs $G_1(z)=g(1-z)(1-z)^b$ with $g(0)=1$. Any other solution with the same tangential leading factor differs by a constant right multiplier; the prescribed leading coefficient $1$ makes that multiplier the identity. For a general parenthesized endpoint, each collision chart from [F2] has the form $\Omega_N=A_S\,d\rho/\rho+\eta(\rho)$ in its radial variable $\rho$, where $A_S=(2\pi i)^{-1}\sum_{i<j\in S}t_{ij}$ and $\eta$ is analytic in $\rho$ with the other corner coordinates as parameters. The same coefficient recursion, inductively in the specified nested collision tree, gives a unique regularized transport after removing $\rho^{A_S}$.

Both $G_0$ and $G_1$ solve the same left differential equation. Differentiating $G_1^{-1}G_0$ therefore gives zero, so their ratio is constant. For $G_\varepsilon(z)=G_0(z)G_0(\varepsilon)^{-1}$, the endpoint expansions and $G_0(\varepsilon)^{-1}=\varepsilon^{-a}f(\varepsilon)^{-1}$ give
$$
\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon^{-b}G_\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)\varepsilon^a
&=\varepsilon^{-b}f(1-\varepsilon)(1-\varepsilon)^a\varepsilon^{-a}f(\varepsilon)^{-1}\varepsilon^a\\
&=\varepsilon^{-b}g(\varepsilon)\varepsilon^b\,\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}\,\varepsilon^{-a}f(\varepsilon)^{-1}\varepsilon^a,
\end{aligned}
$$
where the second equality follows from $G_1(1-\varepsilon)\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}=G_0(1-\varepsilon)$. In each degree, $f(\varepsilon)^{-1}-1$ and $g(\varepsilon)-1$ are $O(\varepsilon)$. Since $a$ and $b$ have positive degree, conjugation by $\varepsilon^{\pm a}$ or $\varepsilon^{\pm b}$ is a finite polynomial in $\log\varepsilon$ in the degree-$N$ quotient. Thus both outside factors in the last expression differ from $1$ by $O(\varepsilon(1+|\log\varepsilon|)^N)$ in each degree, which tends to zero; the limit is $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}$.

Let $T_K$ be the one-in one-out tangle obtained by cutting the chosen monotone arc of $K$, and let $Q$ be the fixed one-in one-out tangle that inserts one maximum-minimum pair. By construction, $K=\operatorname{cl}(T_K)$, $H=\operatorname{cl}(Q)$, and $K^+=\operatorname{cl}(Q\circ T_K)$. Applying [F3] gives $Z(K^+)=Z(H)\#Z(K)=Z(H)Z(K)$ in the completed closed diagram algebra. The degree-zero term of $Z(H)$ is $1$, so its inverse exists degreewise. Since $r(K^+)=r(K)+1$ and connected-sum multiplication is commutative, $I(K^+)=Z(H)Z(K)Z(H)^{-r(K)-1}=Z(K)Z(H)^{-r(K)}=I(K)$. Deleting a standard hump is the inverse equality.

Use coordinates $(z,t)\in\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ on oriented $\mathbb R^3$, with $t$ increasing upward. A knot is a smooth embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ with the orientation of $S^1$. A strict Morse presentation is one for which $t|_K$ has nondegenerate critical points, meaning its second derivative in a local coordinate is nonzero there, and pairwise distinct critical values. Write $t_{\min}:=\min_{x\in K}t(x)$, $t_{\max}:=\max_{x\in K}t(x)$, and $r(K)$ for the number of local maxima. A parenthesized $q$-braid is a smooth braid with $q$ strands, each strictly increasing in $t$, together with an ordered binary parenthesization of its lower endpoints and an ordered binary parenthesization of its upper endpoints.

For $n\ge0$, a degree-$n$ chord diagram is an oriented circle with $n$ disjoint unordered pairs of distinct points, called chords. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr}}$ be the rational vector space on these diagrams modulo 4T, and let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}}$ be its quotient by 1T as well. A 4T relation fixes one chord $pq$ and another chord endpoint $r$, moves the other endpoint of the second chord to just before or after $p$ and just before or after $q$, and takes the alternating sum of those four diagrams. A chord is isolated when it intersects no other chord, where intersection means that chord endpoints alternate around the circle; 1T sets every such diagram to zero. Put $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{fr/un}}_{\mathbb C}:=\prod_{n\ge0}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr/un}}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C)$, with multiplication induced by connected sum of diagrams and unit the empty diagram. For $q$ ordered upward strands, let $\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q)$ be the completion of the associative algebra generated by $t_{ij}=t_{ji}$ for $1\le i<j\le q$, with relations $[t_{ij},t_{kl}]=0$ when $i,j,k,l$ are distinct and $[t_{ij},t_{ik}+t_{jk}]=0$ when $i,j,k$ are distinct. The generator $t_{ij}$ is a horizontal chord joining strands $i$ and $j$; multiplication stacks diagrams from bottom to top.

More generally, a compact strict Morse tangle $T$ is a compact oriented smooth one-dimensional submanifold of $\mathbb C\times[a,b]$, with distinct boundary points on the planes $t=a$ and $t=b$, transverse to those planes, and with nondegenerate interior critical points of height having distinct critical values. A tangle chord diagram is a finite set of unordered pairs of distinct interior points on the oriented tangle skeleton. Its 4T relation is the same local alternating relation as above on the skeleton. The unframed tangle quotient also sets to zero any chord whose endpoints are consecutive in the order along the same skeleton component; for a circle the order is cyclic and for an arc it is linear. The completed degreewise tangle diagram space is denoted $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}(T)$.

The unframed configuration series of a strict Morse presentation $K$ is the formal degreewise series
$$
Z(K):=\sum_{m\ge0}\frac1{(2\pi i)^m}\int_{t_{\min}<t_m<\cdots<t_1<t_{\max}}\ \sum_{P}(-1)^{\downarrow(P)}[D_P]_{\mathrm{un}}\bigwedge_{j=1}^m\frac{dz_j-dz'_j}{z_j-z'_j}\ \in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}.
$$
The ordered simplex is divided into chambers by the critical values of $t|_K$. In each chamber, $P$ ranges over choices, at each level $t_j$, of an unordered pair of distinct points $(z_j,t_j),(z'_j,t_j)$ of $K$. The diagram $D_P$ joins the corresponding preimages on the oriented parameter circle. The integer $\downarrow(P)$ counts endpoints at which $t$ decreases along the orientation of $K$. The differential form is pulled back to the chamber by the selected local branches. The degree-zero term is the empty diagram with coefficient $1$; the displayed integrals are interpreted as improper integrals on each chamber.

For a compact strict Morse tangle $T$, $Z(T)$ is given by the same formula with $T$ in place of $K$, the interval $(a,b)$ in place of $(t_{\min},t_{\max})$, the chord diagrams on the tangle skeleton in place of circle diagrams, and the corresponding unframed tangle quotient in place of $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}$. A parenthesized braid is a special case with no interior critical points.

For a parenthesized braid path $\gamma$ in the configuration space of $q$ distinct complex points, define its Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov (KZ) series by the degreewise iterated-integral holonomy of
$$\Omega_q=\frac1{2\pi i}\sum_{1\le i<j\le q}t_{ij}\,d\log(z_i-z_j).$$
Explicitly, if $\gamma:[0,1]\to\operatorname{Conf}_q(\mathbb C)$ is an ordinary path with noncolliding endpoints, its holonomy is
$$1+\sum_{m\ge1}\int_{0<t_m<\cdots<t_1<1}\gamma^*\Omega_q(t_1)\cdots\gamma^*\Omega_q(t_m).$$
A tangential endpoint is a limiting collision configuration together with a specified nonzero first-order direction of approach for each colliding cluster. When endpoints have such clusters prescribed by the parenthesizations, the holonomy is the constant term after removing the local logarithmic factors $\exp(t_{ij}\log\varepsilon/(2\pi i))$ at each tangential endpoint. A change between the two parenthesizations of three consecutive strands is encoded by the regularized transport $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}$.

For parenthesized braids the KZ holonomy takes values in the framed strand algebra, where only tangled 4T is imposed; passing from a closed framed strand diagram to an unframed knot applies the quotient by isolated-chord 1T. Fix a standard hump $H$ by starting with the two-critical-point unknot and inserting one local birth of a maximum-minimum pair; thus $H$ has two local maxima. The normalized unframed Kontsevich series of $K$ is
$$
I(K):=Z(K)\,Z(H)^{-r(K)}\in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C},
$$
The normalization uses one copy of $Z(H)$ for each local maximum; its degree-zero term is $1$, so its inverse is interpreted in the product completion. This definition makes no assertion that the unnormalized KZ coefficients are rational or that equal Kontsevich series separate knot types.

The following figure illustrates the positive Artin generator $\sigma_1$ and parenthesization conventions. Height increases upward, the right-bottom strand is the overstrand under the determinant crossing convention, and the labels at the ends record the ordered parenthesizations; no proof below relies on the drawing.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.82,thick]
  \draw (2,0) -- (2,3);
  \draw[very thick] (1,0) -- (0.5,1.5) -- (0,3);
  \draw (0,0) -- (0.48,1.44);
  \draw (0.52,1.56) -- (1,3);
  \node at (1,-0.32) {$((1\ 2)\ 3)$};
  \node at (1,3.32) {$((2\ 1)\ 3)$};
  \node at (1.2,2.55) {$\sigma_1$};
  \node at (2.45,1.5) {$t$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and $C=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ a finitely generated free $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ complex. Choose a finite homogeneous basis $\{x_r\}$, with $M(x_r)$ and Alexander filtration $A(x_r)$. The translate $U^k x_r$ has Maslov grading $M(x_r)-2k$ and filtration coordinates $(i,j)=(-k,A(x_r)-k)$. The total homology is $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$; use the standard normalization in which its Maslov-zero tower generator first appears at algebraic filtration level $i=0$, and denote it by $\xi_K$.

For $t\in[0,2]$ and a nonzero finite chain $z$, define
$$ F_t(U^k x_r)=(1-t/2)(-k)+(t/2)(A(x_r)-k),\qquad F_t(z)=\max\{F_t(U^k x_r):U^k x_r\text{ has nonzero coefficient in }z\}. $$
Let $\mathcal Z_0(C)$ be the set of Maslov-zero cycles representing $\xi_K$. Set
$$ \nu_t(C)=\min_{z\in\mathcal Z_0(C)}F_t(z),\qquad \Upsilon_K(t)=-2\nu_t(C). $$
The minimum is over cycles representing the normalized homology generator, not over individual basis terms. For comparison, let $C^-(K)$ be the $\mathbb F_2[U]$-span of the chosen basis and form its $t$-modified complex over the ring $\mathcal R$ of formal sums $\sum_{\alpha\in S}c_\alpha v^\alpha$ whose support $S\subset[0,\infty)$ is well-ordered (every nonempty subset of $S$ has a least element). The coefficient extension uses $U=v^2$. In the extended Laurent complex, $v$ lowers both filtration coordinates by $1/2$ and Maslov grading by one, so a diagonal $U$-translation lowers the extended $t$-grading by two. On arbitrary homogeneous Laurent terms this grading is $M-t(j-i)$; the formula $M-tA$ below is specified on the chosen generators at $i=0$. A homogeneous generator $x$ has $t$-grading $M(x)-tA(x)$, extended by $\operatorname{gr}_t(v^\alpha x)=\operatorname{gr}_t(x)-\alpha$. If a term $U^k y$ occurs in $\partial x$, its $t$-modified differential coefficient is $v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}$; thus for $\partial x=\sum_y c_{xy}U^{(M(y)-M(x)+1)/2}y$, define $\partial_t x=\sum_y c_{xy}v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}y$. This differential lowers $t$-grading by one. The comparison between its non-torsion tower grading and the finite cycle minimum is the separate filtered tower-splitting claim.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere, with chosen minimum-genus oriented Seifert surfaces. A normalized $CFK^\infty(K)$ is a free finite-rank chain complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ with two integer filtrations $(i,j)$, where multiplication by $U$ lowers both coordinates by one. Give the connected sum $K\#J$ the fixed oriented gluing convention and the sum filtrations and Maslov/Alexander gradings. Then $CFK^\infty(K\#J)$ is bifiltered chain homotopy equivalent to $CFK^\infty(K)\otimes_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}CFK^\infty(J)$, with an equivalence and homotopies preserving both filtration coordinates. Moreover, the normalized finite filtered hat complex of $K\#J$ is filtered chain homotopy equivalent to $C_K\otimes C_J$ with tensor filtration $F_s(C_K\otimes C_J)=\sum_{p+q\le s}F_pC_K\otimes F_qC_J$. Consequently,
$$\tau(K\#J)=\tau(K)+\tau(J).$$

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C(K)=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ have a finite homogeneous basis $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ with Maslov grading $M(x_r)$ and Alexander filtration $A(x_r)$. Let $C^-(K)$ be the subcomplex spanned over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by $U^n x_r$ for $n\ge0$, with $M(U^n x_r)=M(x_r)-2n$ and $A(U^n x_r)=A(x_r)-n$, and assume $H_*(C^-(K))\cong\mathbb F_2[U]$ with generator in Maslov degree zero. For each integer $s$, let $\mathcal A(K,s)$ be the subcomplex spanned over $\mathbb F_2$ by those terms $U^n x_r$ with $n\ge0$ and $A(x_r)-n\le s$. For any Maslov-graded $\mathbb F_2[U]$ complex $D$, let $\delta(D)$ be the maximal Maslov grading of a homogeneous non-torsion class in $H_*(D)$, with $\delta(D)=-\infty$ if no such class exists. Define $\nu^-(K)$ to be the least integer $s$ for which $\delta(\mathcal A(K,s))=0$. Then
$$ 0\le \nu^-(K)\le g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K), $$
where $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ is the minimum genus of a smooth compact connected oriented properly embedded surface in the four-ball bounded by $K$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere and let $B^4$ be the standard four-ball with boundary $S^3$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable locally flat topologically properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. For each such surface, its genus $g(F)$ is the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$. Define the smooth slice genus and the locally flat topological slice genus by

$$
g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K),\qquad g_4^{\mathrm{top}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K).
$$

Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. Let $F$ be a compact connected oriented Seifert surface with boundary $K$, and let $\mathcal H=(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,w,z)$ be an admissible doubly pointed Heegaard diagram representing $(K,F)$. The associated one-pointed hat chain complex $\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is the finite-dimensional chain complex over $\mathbb F_2$ obtained from the minus complex by setting its basepoint variable to zero; its differential counts index-one disks with zero multiplicity at $w$. Assume for this specified data that the differential is nonincreasing in the Alexander filtration, that the absolute Alexander formula below takes integer values, and that $H(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))\cong\mathbb F_2$. Give a generator $\mathbf x$ its absolute Alexander filtration
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field assigned to $\mathbf x$ by the pointed Morse construction, with its prescribed boundary data near the two basepoints; $c_1$ is the first Chern class of the oriented plane field perpendicular to that vector field. To form the zero-framed surgery, remove a tubular neighborhood of $K$ and glue in a solid torus whose meridian is the longitude induced by $F$. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by deleting a boundary collar of $F$ and capping its longitude by the meridian disk of that solid torus. This is the standard integer normalization, with the one-generator diagram of the standard unknot at filtration zero. The subcomplex $F_s\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is spanned by generators of Alexander filtration at most $s$.

More generally, a finite integer-filtered chain complex is a finite-dimensional chain complex $C$ over $\mathbb F_2$ with subcomplexes $F_sC$ such that $F_sC=0$ for all sufficiently small integers $s$ and $F_sC=C$ for all sufficiently large integers $s$. If $H(C)\cong\mathbb F_2$, define
$$\tau(C):=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z:\operatorname{im}(H(F_sC)\longrightarrow H(C))\ne0\}.$$
For the fixed diagram and surface above, write $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)=\tau(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H),F_*\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))$. Once diagram and surface independence is proved, their common value is the knot invariant $\tau(K)$. Until that comparison is proved, $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)$ denotes only the value for the specified data.

Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $F$ be a compact connected oriented surface embedded in $S^3$ with boundary $K$ and minimum possible genus; write $g(K)=\operatorname{genus}(F)$. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. For an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram $\mathcal H$ compatible with $(K,F)$, define $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ by the same restriction to a single variable action. Write $CFK^-(K)$ for the full filtered complex of an admissible doubly-pointed diagram. The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

For the absolute Alexander normalization, let $\mathcal H_1$ be an admissible doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(K,F)$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ of $\mathcal H_1$, set
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned to this generator by the pointed Heegaard construction: it is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field obtained from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, after extending the field across small balls around the critical points. Its first Chern class is that of the oriented plane field orthogonal to this vector field. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached in zero-framed surgery on $K$. Let $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from the doubly-pointed complex $C^-_U(\mathcal H_1)$ by quotienting by its sole variable $U$, with this $A_F$ normalization.

Then $C^-_U(G)$ and $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving relative Maslov grading and the $A_F$ filtration, and their Alexander-associated-graded minus complexes are chain homotopy equivalent. For any two grids of $K$, the resulting normalized filtered complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. If $\widetilde{GH}(G)$ denotes the homology of the tilde grid complex over $\mathbb F_2$, then
$$\widetilde{GH}(G)\cong\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)},$$
where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal H$ be any admissible $2k$-pointed Heegaard diagram for an oriented knot in $S^3$, with transverse attaching curves, product tori, and marked points as specified in the pointed-data definition. Admissibility means every nonzero periodic domain with all $w$-multiplicities zero has both positive and negative region coefficients. There is a smooth path $\mathbb J=(J_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$, constant near its endpoints and chosen among perturbations for which all holomorphic-strip representatives used in the differential have nonnegative local multiplicity at every marked point, such that the linearized Cauchy–Riemann operator is surjective for every Maslov-index-$1$ strip class with all $w$-multiplicities nonnegative. Each corresponding moduli space modulo translation is finite. For every Maslov-index-$2$ class with all $w$-multiplicities nonnegative, the compactification of the one-dimensional moduli space modulo translation has as codimension-one boundary broken pairs of index-one strips meeting at an intermediate generator and disk bubbles whose entire boundary lies on one of the product tori (the boundary-degeneration strata). Gluing gives a collar at every broken end, and the boundary-degeneration contributions cancel modulo two in the differential-square count. No sphere bubbling or escape through a nonzero periodic domain gives an additional codimension-one end. Consequently the disk-count differential in the pointed-data definition squares to zero and preserves its Alexander filtration.

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C(K)=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be its normalized bifiltered complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$. The complex of the reverse mirror $-K$ is filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to the dual complex $C(K)^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}(C(K),\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}])$, with dual differential $d\phi(x)=\phi(\partial x)$ and dual basis elements at negated bifiltration coordinates. There is also a Maslov-graded filtered-chain-homotopy equivalence from $C(K)$ to the complex obtained by exchanging the algebraic and Alexander filtrations. These are distinct symmetries: duality negates both filtration coordinates, while conjugation exchanges them.

Fix the orientation-reversing reflection $r:S^3\to S^3$ chosen for the mirror convention in the oriented connected-sum definition. If $K$ is a smooth oriented knot, its mirror $r(K)$ carries the orientation induced from $K$ by $r$. The reverse mirror of $K$, denoted $K^\dagger$, is the image $r(K)$ with its knot orientation reversed. Thus $K^\dagger$ changes both the ambient orientation convention and the orientation of the knot.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $F$ be a fixed minimum-genus oriented Seifert surface, and let $\mathcal H_0,\mathcal H_1$ be admissible doubly pointed Heegaard diagrams for the same pair $(K,F)$ whose hat complexes have total homology $\mathbb F_2$ and the same absolute Alexander normalization. Their diagramwise thresholds agree. Moreover, every grid presentation of $(K,F)$ gives this same value after the full filtered grid complex is converted to the normalized singly pointed model, with all basepoint-variable and stabilization factors accounted for. The common value is $\tau(K)$.

Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $F$ be a compact connected oriented surface embedded in $S^3$ with boundary $K$ and minimum possible genus; write $g(K)=\operatorname{genus}(F)$. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. For an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram $\mathcal H$ compatible with $(K,F)$, define $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ by the same restriction to a single variable action. The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

For the absolute Alexander normalization, let $\mathcal H_1$ be an admissible doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(K,F)$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ of $\mathcal H_1$, set
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned to this generator by the pointed Heegaard construction: it is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field obtained from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, after extending the field across small balls around the critical points. Its first Chern class is that of the oriented plane field orthogonal to this vector field. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached in zero-framed surgery on $K$. Let $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from the doubly-pointed complex $C^-_U(\mathcal H_1)$ by quotienting by its sole variable $U$, with this $A_F$ normalization.

Then $C^-_U(G)$ and $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving relative Maslov grading and the $A_F$ filtration, and their Alexander-associated-graded minus complexes are chain homotopy equivalent. For any two grids of $K$, the resulting normalized filtered complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. If $\widetilde{GH}(G)$ denotes the homology of the tilde grid complex over $\mathbb F_2$, then
$$\widetilde{GH}(G)\cong\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)},$$
where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

Let $C=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be the finite-rank free $\Lambda=\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ knot Floer complex of a smooth oriented knot, with its Maslov grading, algebraic filtration $i$, Alexander filtration $j$, and weighted filtration $F_t=(1-t/2)i+(t/2)j$ for a fixed $t\in[0,2]$. derivations.claim: By [F1], each fixed Maslov-zero cycle has filtration equal to the maximum of finitely many affine functions of $t$, and there are finitely many such cycles. Thus $\Upsilon_K$ is piecewise linear with finitely many breakpoints. The supplied model comparison [F8] makes this calculation a knot invariant. At $t=0$, $F_0$ is the algebraic filtration; the normalization in [F1] says the tower generator first appears at level zero, so $\nu_0=0$ and $\Upsilon_K(0)=0$. Exchanging the two bifiltration coordinates sends $F_t$ to $F_{2-t}$; [F2] therefore gives $\Upsilon_K(t)=\Upsilon_K(2-t)$.

Under the supplied geometric tensor comparison [F5], the connected-sum complex is the convolution-filtered Laurent tensor product. For a fixed $t$, apply the proved filtered splitting [F4] separately to the two factors. Their rank-one summands tensor to a zero-differential tower whose normalized generator has filtration $
u_t(K)+
u_t(J)$. Every other tensor summand contains an acyclic Laurent factor and is acyclic. To justify that last assertion without a filtered contraction assumption, normalize the factor's basis to Maslov degrees zero and one: its differential is given by finite binary matrices from degree one to zero and from degree zero to $U$ times degree one. Acyclicity makes the resulting finite parity complex acyclic, so finite vector-space complements give a contracting homotopy; the Laurent degree shifts insert only powers of $U$ or $U^{-1}$ to make it a chain homotopy. Tensoring this contraction with any other complex is a contraction, since the two cross terms cancel over $\mathbb F_2$. Thus only the displayed tower carries total homology. The splitting is filtered, so no representative of its nonzero class can have a smaller filtration than that tower generator. This proves $
u_t(K\#J)=
u_t(K)+
u_t(J)$ and Upsilon additivity.

By the actual normalized geometric duality [F2], the reverse-mirror complex is the filtered dual. Dualize the fixed-$t$ filtered splitting in [F4]. A filtration-preserving change of basis with filtration-preserving inverse has the same property after dualizing and negating the basis filtrations. The dual of the minimizing tower has normalized generator at filtration $-\nu_t(K)$. The dual complementary factor is acyclic, because the unfiltered finite Laurent contraction in step 1.2 dualizes to a contraction. Therefore the dual minimax equals $-\nu_t(K)$, and $\Upsilon_{-K}(t)=-\Upsilon_K(t)$. This uses no unproved identification of the homology of a dual torsion module.

First derive the actual minus normalization from [F6]. Since $B$ is finite free over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ with homogeneous generators, its chain groups vanish above a fixed Maslov degree. The exact sequence $0\to UB\to B\to B/UB\to0$ and $H(B/UB)=\mathbb F_2$ in degree zero imply that multiplication by $U$ is an isomorphism between adjacent even-degree homology groups below zero and between adjacent odd-degree groups; boundedness above gives $H_{>0}(B)=0$, $H_0(B)=\mathbb F_2$, and all odd groups zero. Thus $H(B)=\mathbb F_2[U]$ generated in degree zero. Every normalized minus cycle projects to the hat generator. Conversely, lift a Maslov-zero hat generator cycle to $c\in B$. Write $\partial c=Ud$; then $\partial d=0$ and $M(d)=1$. Since $H_1(B)=0$, write $d=\partial e$. The polynomial cycle $c+Ue$ lifts the SAME hat cycle and has the same leading $i=0$ terms. Therefore the least Alexander level among the $i=0$ parts of normalized minus cycles is exactly $\tau(K)$. Every normalized minus representative has a nonzero $i=0$ part, since a representative wholly in $UB$ would make the top homology generator $U$-divisible. The finite Maslov-zero Laurent cycle set admits a common positive $t$ interval in which any term with $i\ge1$ excludes a cycle from minimizing, and the maximum on a cycle with $i\le0$ comes only from its $i=0$ terms. Hence $\nu_t(K)=t\tau(K)/2$ on that interval and $\Upsilon'_K(0+)=-\tau(K)$. No genus estimate is used.

Let $s=\nu^-(K)$ as defined in [F9], and put $g=g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$. Since $\delta(\mathcal A(K,s))=0$, there is a non-torsion homology class of Maslov grading zero represented by a cycle $z$ in $\mathcal A(K,s)$. The total homology is $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$; use the standard normalization in which its Maslov-zero tower generator first appears at algebraic filtration level $i=0$, and denote it by $\xi_K$.

For $t\in[0,2]$ and a nonzero finite chain $z$, define
$$ F_t(U^k x_r)=(1-t/2)(-k)+(t/2)(A(x_r)-k),\qquad F_t(z)=\max\{F_t(U^k x_r):U^k x_r\text{ has nonzero coefficient in }z\}. $$
Let $\mathcal Z_0(C)$ be the set of Maslov-zero cycles representing $\xi_K$. Set
$$ \nu_t(C)=\min_{z\in\mathcal Z_0(C)}F_t(z),\qquad \Upsilon_K(t)=-2\nu_t(C). $$
The minimum is over cycles representing the normalized homology generator, not over individual basis terms. For comparison, let $C^-(K)$ be the $\mathbb F_2[U]$-span of the chosen basis and form its $t$-modified complex over the ring $\mathcal R$ of formal sums $\sum_{\alpha\in S}c_\alpha v^\alpha$ whose support $S\subset[0,\infty)$ is well-ordered (every nonempty subset of $S$ has a least element). The coefficient extension uses $U=v^2$. In the extended Laurent complex, $v$ lowers both filtration coordinates by $1/2$ and Maslov grading by one, so a diagonal $U$-translation lowers the extended $t$-grading by two. On arbitrary homogeneous Laurent terms this grading is $M-t(j-i)$; the formula $M-tA$ below is specified on the chosen generators at $i=0$. A homogeneous generator $x$ has $t$-grading $M(x)-tA(x)$, extended by $\operatorname{gr}_t(v^\alpha x)=\operatorname{gr}_t(x)-\alpha$. If a term $U^k y$ occurs in $\partial x$, its $t$-modified differential coefficient is $v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}$; thus for $\partial x=\sum_y c_{xy}U^{(M(y)-M(x)+1)/2}y$, define $\partial_t x=\sum_y c_{xy}v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}y$.
